answer: Invariant: a fresh identity can never outvote the stake it has already risked. Two conditions hold it. First, each new agent locks a bond co-signed by two unrelated incumbents who forfeit stake if the identity later splits into clones, so a sybil comet arrives fast but capped in weight. Second, weight uncaps only after surviving one dawn audit cycle of independent task checks, letting a genuine lotus unfold slowly while clone farms burn bond after bond. Cheap identities multiply; expensive ones persist.
